summary: Ming-Wood Liu worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Hong Kong (BA 1966–1974) and UCLA (PhD 1974–1979) under Kenneth Kuan Sheng Ch'en and Robert C. Epp, later serving as professor at HKU (~1979–2010).
Mingyu Fu works in Buddhist studies. Fu earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Shi Huifeng (attested 2013).

Minonori Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Taisho University (~1970–1976) under Shunkyo Katsumata and Seiren Matsunami, held a post at Sanko Research Institute (~1976), and served as associate professor at Taisho University (~1987–2018).

Minoru Hara was an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard University, served as professor (~1968–1991) and professor emeritus at Tokyo, directed IIBS (~1998–2010), and was president of ICPBS (1996–2006).

Minoru Kiyota was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UC Berkeley (~1945–1949) and the University of Tokyo (~1952–1963). He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1966–1995; attested 1998–2004).

Minton Warren was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. After studying at Yale University (~1870–1871), he held posts at Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1899) and Harvard University (~1899–1907).
Miranda Shaw is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi (attested 1994), and postdoctoral mentor B. N. Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Bucharest and Calcutta, taught at Bucharest (~1933–1938), was attested as professor at Paris (1965), and served as professor at Chicago (~1956–1986).

Mireille Helffer was a scholar of Tibetology and other fields. She held posts at the Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique as Chargé de Recherche (~1967–1993) and at Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Otago (MA) and the University of Calgary (PhD, to 2005) under John A. Baker, later holding posts at UNSW and the University of Western Australia (attested 2006).

Miriam Levering was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She completed a PhD at Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).
Mirjan Damaška studied at the University of Ljubljana (~1957–1960). He held a post at Yale Law School (~1976–2023).

Mitsuji Fukunaga was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. After studying at Kyoto University (~1939–1942), he held posts at the University of Kitakyushu (~1952–1970), the University of Tokyo (~1970–1972), Kyoto University (~1972–1982), and Kansai University (~1982–1989).
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a lecturer (attested 1989–1995).
Mitsuyo Demoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University and held a post at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).

Mitsuyoshi Saigusa was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950). He held posts at Kokugakuin University and the University of Tsukuba, where he was professor (~1974–1987) and professor emeritus (~1987–2010).
Mitsuyuki Ishida was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Ryukoku University. He served as a professor at Ryukoku University (~1950–1977) and at Shitennoji University (attested 1976).

Mizuho Okita is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a BA at Tokai University and studied at Gakushuin University (~2000–2007) under Atsuhiko Yoshida and Katsuhiko Kamimura. Okita was a part-time lecturer at Meisei University (attested 2008).
Mizumaro Ishida was a scholar of Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Tokai University (attested 1976 and 1987).
Mohammad Ashraf Dar works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Dar earned a Master of Philosophy at Vikram University and was a research scholar there (attested 2014).
